scope: CPU-only; reads completed root-owned runtime artifacts. No host classifier imported, no ownership check, no GPU or driver action.
argument_scope: All160 retained8-byte argument images encode the one allocated output pointer; pinned reviewed host retains that object through synchronous completion. HIP journal records function/context/timing/result, not raw native argument buffers independently of the host.
library_scope: Complete retained maps and host start/terminal hash records bind both pinned runtime libraries. Separate post-run file-only rehash is retained alongside this audit when available; no in-memory code attestation is claimed.
limits: An explicit calibration PC need not differ from its before snapshot; this is separate from the NOP freshness criterion.
A later spontaneous trap may supersede explicit return-PC evidence. If the final PC is outside the accepted aligned plateau range, calibration fails; later aligned plateau heads remain accepted.
Last visible TTMP state is not a complete trap history or event count.
The tag snapshot window is wider than the TTMP plateau. Fresh-PC and copy evidence co-occur in one invocation; this does not prove one uniquely identified trap caused the copy.
This is a tagged-register exposure probe, not a native DW replay or training-stability test.
Per-symbol loaded PCs are reconstructed from shader-computed packet addresses and the pinned native image; function handles are opaque and are not treated as code addresses.
Module-base agreement across all160 calls supports the current image join; it does not reconstruct older trap history.
No fresh spontaneous copy in this bounded probe does not establish a handler fix or training stability.
